thread.title: Asian stocks sink, led by Apple suppliers, on Trump’s latest tariff threat

author: Dow Jones Newswire
title: Asian stocks sink, led by Apple suppliers, on Trump’s latest tariff threat
text:
Asian stocks dropped Tuesday following President Donald Trump’s announcement of potentially $200 billion in additional tariffs against imports from China.
In Japan, the yen jumped on that news, and the Nikkei NIK, -0.87% was off almost 1%. Export-related stocks slid, with Komatsu 6301, -1.50% shedding 1.5% while Honda 7267, -0.95% was down 0.9%. The dollar USDJPY, -0.64% was down 0.4% versus the yen at ¥110.13.
China stocks opened sharply lower following Monday’s holiday and amid increased trade tensions with the U.S. The Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, -2.60% was off 2.2% in early trading and the Shenzhen Composite 399106, -3.94% was off 2%. The Shanghai benchmark has fallen three straight days and four consecutive weeks, finishing Friday at a 21-month low.
Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.05% suppliers’ stocks were hit hard around the region, despite a report that U.S. tariffs would spare iPhones produced in China. IPhone-camera maker Cowell Holdings 1415, -10.47% skidded 10% in Hong Kong to fresh record lows, while smartphone-lens maker Sunny Optical 2382, -5.18% pulled back a further 4.4% and acoustics firm AAC Technologies 2018, -3.33% fell 2.8%. In Taiwan, Sunny peer Largan Precision 3008, -4.25% was off 4.2%. Apple product assembler Hon Hai Precision Industry 2317, -2.00% dropped 2%. Indexes in Hong Kong HSI, -1.96% and Taiwan Y9999, -1.33% were each down more than 1%.
Meanwhile, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 XJO, +0.36% was up 0.5% as the Aussie dollar fell on the trade talk. Korea’s benchmark dipped SEU, -0.67% and New Zealand’s NZX NZ50GR, -0.53% was down about 0.3%.
